data: Synthetic only: sample book pages printed by real Chromium, drawn digits as written answers, photos made by a perspective map, blur and JPEG.

evidence.what: SCAN_MATRIX_OUT=<file> npx vitest run src/lib/scan-binding-chromium.test.ts -t "every scale". 24 real pages (U4, U16, U26), page fill 50% to 95%, upright, rotated 7 degrees and tilted, calibrated on the normalized upload bytes and checked among all 24 pages. nearTwinsAlsoStoppedBySheet: pairs that only the QR code stopped, asked again with the sheet check alone, as if that page's code were pasted on the sheet.
The two #456 cases with the sheet check switched off, as on main: both calibrate. Then the PR #637 review's glare case on 08981a79: the job saves crops at 0.1 and 0.05 of the print's contrast.

The sheet check's scores for each spot where near twins print differently, on right pages and read as the twin, with the print-against-print fits that decide which pages are near twins, and the glare cases. The cutoffs in scan-calibration.ts come from here.
One crop job over 200 of the child's other page images, a few at a time (on 08981a79 this took about 2.21 GB, per the PR #637 review). rss is the whole test process, 452 MB before the job starts.

limits: No real camera photo, curled saddle-stitched page or real handwriting. Glare is drawn as lowered contrast. Candidates are the child's printed pages of the same page type. Near twins are pages that hold 75% of this page's print; a sheet of a less similar page over a small part of this one is checked only by the page comparison. One spot of five may stay unclear, so a sheet over a single digit that looks like its twin at that resolution can pass.
